st.headline: Singapore’s DayOne said to weigh options for US IPO after data centre rout
st.teaser: Deliberations are ongoing and DayOne has not made any final decisions, people familiar with the matter said.
fullText: DayOne Data Centers is weighing options for its US initial public offering , including a potential delay or size cut, as volatility around data centres increases, according to people familiar with the matter.

While Singapore-based DayOne has been waiting for the right window to launch the IPO, it has also been considering the possibility of pushing back the share sale until the market recovers, the people said.
Other options include going ahead with a smaller listing that may raise US$2.5 billion (S$3.2 billion) to US$3 billion, roughly half of what it had originally aimed for, the people said.
DayOne, whose backers include Coatue and Hillhouse, is continuing to engage with potential investors and still wants to move forward as soon as the market allows, the people said.
The company was initially considering raising as much as US$5 billion from the listing as soon as the fourth quarter, people familiar with the matter said previously.
It had been eyeing a valuation of about US$20 billion, the people have said.

Deliberations are ongoing and DayOne has not made any final decisions, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. The company could still opt to move ahead with the offering in the coming weeks, according to the people.

While data centres have drawn global investor demand amid a boom in sectors related to artificial intelligence, a more negative sentiment has started to have ripple effects on IPOs. DayOne has been raising billions of dollars in private funding rounds as it seeks capital to build out its pipeline.

Australian data centre company Firmus Grid pulled its roughly US$5 billion IPO when investors balked at the valuation it sought, while AirTrunk, which also operates data centres, delayed a planned real estate investment trust IPO in Singapore to 2027.

South Korean digital infrastructure company Elice plunged 32% in its Seoul trading debut on Oct 20. Coreweave’s shares have more than halved since their May peak, and Nscale is facing pushback over its target IPO valuation, Bloomberg News reported.
On Oct 21, shares of Australian data center operator Nextdc plummeted after it cut earnings guidance.

Some investors are hoping that the recent market volatility will pass after the US midterm elections on Nov 3. They are also looking ahead to the performance of Anthropic PBC’s upcoming listing as an important gauge of sentiment toward the AI sector.

DayOne filed for a US IPO earlier in October. The offering is being led by Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan Chase & Co., Bank of America and Citigroup IFR reported on Oct 19 that DayOne was gathering more investor feedback before launching the share sale.
DayOne is running or developing data centres in Singapore, Malaysia , Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain.
Other backers include GDS Holdings, the SoftBank Vision Fund and Citadel’s Ken Griffin. BLOOMBERG

cna.headline: BOJ's Himino signals readiness to raise borrowing costs
cna.teaser: BOJ's Himino signals readiness to raise borrowing costs
fullText: TOKYO, Oct 21 : Japan's underlying inflation is quite close to the central bank's 2 per cent target and financial conditions remain loose, Deputy Bank of Japan Governor Ryozo Himino said on Wednesday, signalling readiness to raise borrowing costs.
While rising fuel and raw material costs are pushing up prices, brisk global AI demand is also putting upward pressure on prices by boosting exports and capital expenditure, Himino told parliament.

"Given medium- and long-term inflation expectations continue to heighten, underlying inflation is quite close to 2 per cent and will likely converge to levels consistent with our price target," Himino said.
"Even after last month's rate hike, financial conditions remain accommodative" as seen in still-low real borrowing costs and strong growth in bank lending, he said.

"Given that inflation risks are high, delaying necessary adjustment to monetary support could materialise such risks and hurt the economy in the long run," Himino said, calling for the need to continue raising interest rates.

mom.headline: Additional Guidance for Employers on Use of 1-Hour PM2.5 Readings to Protect Outdoor Workers During Haze
mom.teaser: 1 The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has issued new guidance on how employers should adjust outdoor work based on the 1-hour PM2.5 readings. This complements the existing guidance based on the PSI forecast, and helps employers respond within the day as air quality changes.
